# Scooping Grasping with Robotic Hand

> A research project by Seunghwan Um, Tae Hyun Bae, and Prof. Hyouk Ryeol Choi at Sungkyunkwan University.

## Overview

This project demonstrates a robotic hand performing a scooping grasping motion — picking up objects from the floor using a natural scooping lift-off.

Controlling scooping motion is extremely challenging for robotic hands with rigid fingertips, because contact with the environment creates constrained (closed-loop) kinematic chains that can damage the system. Soft fingertips trade off grasping force and positional accuracy.

## Key Contribution

Using fingertip force-torque sensors attached to an AIDIN Robotics hand, we solved this problem without soft fingertips:

1. **Fingertip Force Transformation**: Each fingertip wrench is measured and transformed to the wrist frame via the kinematic chain.
2. **Wrist Wrench Aggregation**: All fingertip wrenches are aggregated and combined with the physical wrist F/T sensor reading.
3. **Compliance Control**: The combined wrench feeds into an impedance controller, enabling the manipulator to react compliantly to both wrist-level and fingertip-level contacts during scooping.

This approach avoids closed-loop chains upon contact, enabling safe interaction against external constraints.
